packages.title: EA PI fugitive-versus-point QA
facts: Pollution Inventory reporting covers point and non-point releases.
Fugitive emissions such as leaks are within permit-wide reporting scope.
Point sources include defined release points such as stacks.
Point and fugitive categories should not be merged without preserving source type.
Site-level industrial releases are not automatically parcel-level land emissions.

packages.title: EA release-estimation-technique hierarchy QA
facts: EA technical guidance supports sampling, flow and concentration based quantification.
Sector guidance may define preferred release-estimation techniques.
Measured and calculated estimates must retain their method labels.
Alternative estimation methods require appropriate justification or agreement.
Method choice affects confidence and comparability.

packages.title: EA cement CEMS-priority QA
facts: Cement/lime/mineral A1 facilities report annual mass releases.
The sector guidance prefers continuous-emissions-monitoring data first.
Periodic monitoring is the next preference.
Mass balance or emission factors are a lower preference where applicable.
Industrial annual release mass must not be inferred from permit presence alone.

packages.title: EA chemicals pollutant-scope QA
facts: Chemicals-sector PI guidance applies to regulated A1 facilities.
Relevant air pollutants include carbon dioxide alongside many non-GHG substances.
Waste-incineration or combustion operations may require additional sector guidance.
Pollutants must retain substance-specific units and scope.
A chemical-site pollutant list is not proof of a parcel emission value.

packages.title: EA refinery source-category QA
facts: Refinery guidance covers process, combustion, wastewater and other source categories.
CO2 sources can include furnaces, boilers, turbines, flares and incinerators.
VOC sources can include storage, handling, vents and fugitive leaks.
Measured and calculated substances are treated differently where guidance specifies.
Source category must be preserved when aggregating refinery releases.

packages.title: EA paper/pulp reporting-scope QA
facts: Paper and pulp A1 facilities submit Pollution Inventory data.
Common releases include air and water pollutants plus off-site waste transfers.
CO2 can arise from specified paper/pulp processes.
Waste transfers use defined waste and recovery/disposal codes.
Waste-transfer quantities are not GHG emissions.

packages.title: ECUK 2025 revision-U3 QA
facts: ECUK 2025 was updated 20 April 2026.
Table U3 was revised for 2017 to 2019 domestic end-use estimates.
The revision corrected an estimation error.
Superseded U3 values should not be mixed with revised values.
End-use estimates are energy-use statistics, not direct GHG measurements.

packages.title: ECUK modelled-end-use QA
facts: ECUK end-use tables estimate how final energy is used.
Many end-use splits are modelled and assumption-dependent.
Domestic assumptions are updated using the English Housing Survey.
Industry and services end-use splits can rely on older reference studies.
Modelled end use must not be represented as meter-measured parcel consumption.

packages.title: ECUK industrial-SIC reference QA
facts: ECUK C3 tables disaggregate industry to 2-digit SIC divisions.
A new reference table is used from 2021 onwards.
Earlier years use the prior reference table.
The newer reference improves bioenergy/waste apportionment and SIC consistency.
A methodology break must be retained in time-series comparisons.

packages.title: ECUK transport-electricity-share QA
facts: Electricity was 2.2% of transport energy consumption in 2024.
The share was 0.7% in 2014.
Growth is linked largely to road-transport electricity use.
Vehicle registration counts are activity context rather than energy consumption itself.
National transport energy shares are not parcel emissions.

packages.title: ECUK transport-intensity alignment QA
facts: June 2026 ECUK work reviews transport-energy-intensity methodology.
Energy-intensity metrics combine energy consumption with passenger or freight activity.
Numerator and denominator coverage are not always perfectly aligned.
The planned update aims to improve alignment by transport mode.
A methodology proposal should not be treated as a final published 2026 series.

packages.title: ECUK 2026 proposed-method QA
facts: June 2026 articles describe planned ECUK 2026 methodology changes.
Industrial end-use changes are intended for September 2026 publication.
Proposed sector definitions remain subject to feedback and implementation.
Provisional impacts are not final ECUK 2026 observations.
Keep current ECUK 2025 values distinct from proposed 2026 methods.

packages.title: NEED median-versus-mean QA
facts: NEED 2026 summarises domestic gas and electricity consumption through 2024.
Domestic NEED focuses on median consumption for typical properties.
Subnational consumption reporting focuses on means for geographic aggregation.
Mean and median are not interchangeable.
Neither statistic alone is a parcel GHG measurement.

packages.title: NEED matched-properties scope QA
facts: Domestic NEED uses properties to which gas/electric meters can be matched.
HMRC Council Tax data are used as the domestic-property population for England and Wales.
AddressBase is used for Scotland.
This differs from meter-centric subnational consumption coverage.
Matched-property analysis must preserve its population definition.

packages.title: NEED-versus-subnational consumption QA
facts: Subnational statistics seek geographic totals for domestic and non-domestic meters.
NEED seeks typical domestic consumption by household/property characteristics.
The two products use different summary statistics and populations.
A few disclosive non-domestic gas meters are excluded from subnational consumption.
Do not combine the two products as if they were one identical measurement frame.

packages.title: ECO4 extension-to-2026 QA
facts: ECO4 is a Great Britain energy-efficiency scheme administered by Ofgem.
The ECO4 Order runs to 31 December 2026.
Delivery guidance was updated in March 2026 for the extension.
Scheme eligibility and obligations are policy/administrative data.
Scheme status does not directly measure household CO2e.

packages.title: ECO4 measure-notification versus emissions QA
facts: ECO4 guidance covers measure/project notification.
It also covers project scores, monitoring, audit and counter-fraud.
Supplier obligations and completed-measure notifications are administrative events.
Estimated savings or scores must not be labelled measured emissions.
Property-level scheme participation requires a separate parcel/source binding gate.

packages.title: ECO4 NMAP cutoff QA
facts: ECO4 New Measures and Products guidance includes innovation routes.
After the 2026 amendment, Innovation Measure and Data Light Measure applications are not accepted after 31 March 2026.
Applications received before the cutoff can still be considered.
Application status is not an emissions observation.
Preserve scheme-version and date rules when using innovation data.

packages.title: Renewables capacity-versus-generation QA
facts: DESNZ renewables statistics separately report capacity and generation.
Quarterly Energy Trends includes renewable capacity and generation.
Regional statistics include sites, installed capacity, generation and load factors.
Installed MW must not be treated as generated MWh.
Neither metric directly provides parcel GHG emissions.

packages.title: Regional renewables disclosure-boundary QA
facts: Regional renewable statistics are annual and compatible with DUKES vintages.
Regional allocation can exclude or group sites for disclosure reasons in downstream natural-capital use.
Country or region sums may differ from UK totals where other-sites categories apply.
Do not infer suppressed site generation.
Site-level renewable generation is not identical to avoided-GHG estimates.

packages.title: Cross-source year/unit/geography guard QA
facts: The source set mixes 2024 data, 2025 data and 2026 publications.
Coverage includes UK, Great Britain and England-only products.
Metrics include households, vehicle kilometres, energy, pollutants, GHG and monetary natural capital.
Units and accounting bases must remain source-specific.
Cross-source joins require explicit year, geography and metric keys.

packages.title: Cross-source parcel-inference guard QA
facts: None of these document-level sources alone establishes a measured parcel GHG value.
National, regional, road-link, facility and household data have different spatial units.
Geometry binding must be a separate verified gate.
Suppressed, modelled or projected values must not be fabricated at parcel level.
Parcel binding confidence remains zero until canonical parcel/source evidence exists.
